question.text: The minimum value of <math><mi>x</mi></math> which satisfies the inequality <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">n</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">x</mi><mo>≥</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">c</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup><mi>x</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>λ</mi></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mi>λ</mi></math> is (use <math><msqrt><mn>2</mn></msqrt><mo>=</mo><mn>1.41</mn></math>)

solution.text:
Using the graphs of sin-1x & cos-1x, we can see that
sin-1x≥cos-1x for x∈12,1
So, the minimum value of x is λ=12
